item.title: Re: Listener of SCP-2137
item.content:encoded:
1) The Foundation realizes that there are a lot of civilians that are onto them; this is why they play things off the way they do, using a bit of misdirection and using Weekly World News to deal with SCPs. They expect these guys and are aware of them. However, it's not a bad idea to look at one.

2) The character either needs to be a techno-master or essentially off-line. If he's using a lot of processing power then he needs to be plugged into the grid, but he can't really be bitcoin-miner if he's off-grid. They're two different mindsets so you need to allow for that.

3) Your choice: There are some psuedo-civilian groups out there, so he could join one of those instead of dying. SCP-2137 could save him, or they could just decide that he's got some solid investigative chops, making him a great agent or a great person to have access to. So there are options.

Overall, I like the idea but you need to decide how you're going to approach him right and have some serious fun with him.

item.title: Re: Listener of SCP-2137
item.content:encoded:
Thanks for the advice, I agree with all of it.

Developing an outline a little more in depth sounds like a good idea.

I also agree that the protagonist being a little more mundane is a good call.

I also thought of an ending that’s better than him just dying:

I think eventually he gets caught, but SCP-2137 has requested that the protagonist not be harmed. The agent that finally stops the protagonist, knows that he can’t let him leave with his memories. But it seems like such a shame for someone who dedicated so much effort into finding the truth to just forget it all. So the agent agrees to answer any three questions the protagonist still has before erasing any memory he has of the Foundation.

This ending would be kind of bittersweet, the protagonist comes out unharmed and ultimately succeeded his mission, but is left without any memory of it.

What do you think? Interesting or does it sound cheesy? Out of character for the foundation, maybe?

Anyone else reading feel free to offer an opinion as well.

In the meantime, I’ll work on constructing an outline.

item.title: Re: Listener of SCP-2137
item.content:encoded:
So mostly what you’ve written here is the premise, but then sorta hand waive away the majority of the article’s content by saying:

This character would then go on a journey trying to access SCP facilities and finding whatever clues he can as a civilian in the SCP universe.

I think before you go much further you should think about what this tale actually looks like.

+ show block
– hide block

Nitpick:

I feel like several things you’ve said are either contradictory or just sorta uninteresting… instead of your protagonist being a “techno master” (by which I assume you meant hacker?) why not make them a lonely person who spends most of their time on the internet… instead of someone who tries to get Bitcoin (which for the most part these seem like tech Bros or finance Bros) make your character more relatable to the everyday reader… someone who has a reason to search out the foundation

Finally, I think your overall concern for this protagonist should tie into that SCP they experienced… instead of them deciding they need to see an anomaly, because why would they even know there were other anomalies?

How would they even discover the foundation? Or how to get to one of the sites? Or breaching a site?

Additionally, I think the ending would be better a little less cliched… “he searched too hard for forbidden knowledge and then died (or lost his mind)” is sorta tropey… try to aim for something not used over and over, think about other ways this could end that would make sense

item.title: Listener of SCP-2137
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Elevator Pitch: I just listened to TheVolgun’s fantastic audio rendition of SCP-2137 and was very fascinated with the article as a whole.

The article mentions that highly secret details of the Foundation were leaked on YouTube and iTunes and the efforts to cover up the iTunes incident were imperfect.

It stands to reason then, that maybe some sheltered person hiding behind a sophisticated proxy, or something, managed to download and listen to the songs without having his memory erased, or even being noticed by the Foundation.

I feel that a story following this character as he becomes obsessed trying to get to the bottom of the SCP foundation would be an interesting read.

Central Narrative: I believe the protagonist of this tale would perhaps be some kind of techno-master who spends hours delving into the internet for obscure media. Someone who would notice a strange new album from Tupac appearing on Beyoncé’s iTunes page before it got taken down. The type of guy whose basement is filled with GPUs mining Bitcoin.

I think it would also make sense for this character to be as “off grid” as possible while still having internet access. So he hears about these songs, that sound a lot like Tupac, that are supposedly revealing deeply hidden truths about the world and he pounces on it. Buys the album without a second thought, backs up the songs on multiple drives, and devotes endless effort to figuring out what they mean.

This character would then go on a journey trying to access SCP facilities and finding whatever clues he can as a civilian in the SCP universe.

Perhaps the story could also alternate between perspectives as foundation agents realize there’s a civilian who’s onto them.

I think ultimately the tale would end with the protagonist learning much more than any typical civilian would ever hope to. Like witnessing one or more SCPs firsthand, but getting killed in the process.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Most tales I’ve read are from the perspective of either Foundation Agents, someone in a GoI, or an SCP. I don’t know of many from the perspective of civilians. I also think the leaks from SCP-2137 are an event ripe for exploration.

Additional Notes: I’m returning to the SCP wiki after a fairly long absence so I’m sure there are things I’ve missed. I originally formatted this post wrong because last time I posted here no such thing existed. So if this idea has been done, or if it’s very similar to another tale, please let me know!
